claim: A genetic variant rs641738 near genes encoding MBOAT7 and TMC4 associates with increased risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD).
source: Recent studies have identified a genetic variant rs641738 near two genes encoding membrane bound O-acyltransferase domain-containing 7 (MBOAT7) and transmembrane channel-like 4 (TMC4) that associate with increased risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), alcohol-related cirrhosis, and liver fibrosis in those infected with viral hepatitis (Buch et al., 2015; Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; Thabet et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies (Buch et al., 2015; Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; Thabet et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017).

claim: The rs641738 variant associates with increased risk of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH).
source: Recent studies have identified a genetic variant rs641738 near two genes encoding membrane bound O-acyltransferase domain-containing 7 (MBOAT7) and transmembrane channel-like 4 (TMC4) that associate with increased risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), alcohol-related cirrhosis, and liver fibrosis in those infected with viral hepatitis (Buch et al., 2015; Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; Thabet et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: The rs641738 variant associates with increased risk of alcohol-related cirrhosis.
source: Recent studies have identified a genetic variant rs641738 near two genes encoding membrane bound O-acyltransferase domain-containing 7 (MBOAT7) and transmembrane channel-like 4 (TMC4) that associate with increased risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), alcohol-related cirrhosis, and liver fibrosis in those infected with viral hepatitis (Buch et al., 2015; Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; Thabet et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: The rs641738 variant associates with increased risk of liver fibrosis in those infected with viral hepatitis.
source: Recent studies have identified a genetic variant rs641738 near two genes encoding membrane bound O-acyltransferase domain-containing 7 (MBOAT7) and transmembrane channel-like 4 (TMC4) that associate with increased risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), alcohol-related cirrhosis, and liver fibrosis in those infected with viral hepatitis (Buch et al., 2015; Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; Thabet et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Based on hepatic expression quantitative trait loci analysis, it has been suggested that MBOAT7 loss of function promotes liver disease progression.
source: Based on hepatic expression quantitative trait loci analysis, it has been suggested that MBOAT7 loss of function promotes liver disease progression (Buch et al., 2015; Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; Thabet et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017), but this has never been formally tested.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies and eQTL analysis.

claim: Mboat7 loss, but not Tmc4, in mice is sufficient to promote the progression of NAFLD in the setting of high fat diet.
source: Here we show that Mboat7 loss, but not Tmc4, in mice is sufficient to promote the progression of NAFLD in the setting of high fat diet.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing that Mboat7 knockdown, but not Tmc4 knockout, promotes hepatic steatosis in high fat diet-fed mice.

claim: Mboat7 loss of function is associated with accumulation of its substrate lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) lipids.
source: Mboat7 loss of function is associated with accumulation of its substrate lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) lipids, and direct administration of LPI promotes hepatic inflammatory and fibrotic transcriptional changes in an Mboat7-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing increased LPI levels in Mboat7 knockdown mice.

claim: Direct administration of LPI promotes hepatic inflammatory and fibrotic transcriptional changes in an Mboat7-dependent manner.
source: Mboat7 loss of function is associated with accumulation of its substrate lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) lipids, and direct administration of LPI promotes hepatic inflammatory and fibrotic transcriptional changes in an Mboat7-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that LPI injection increases inflammatory and fibrotic gene expression in Mboat7 knockdown mice but not control mice.

claim: MBOAT7-driven acylation of LPI lipids suppresses the progression of NAFLD.
source: These studies reveal a novel role for MBOAT7-driven acylation of LPI lipids in suppressing the progression of NAFLD.
evidence: The claim is supported by the overall experimental findings showing that loss of Mboat7 promotes NAFLD progression and LPI accumulation.

claim: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) affects roughly one-third of adults in the United States.
source: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is an increasingly common condition that affects roughly one-third of adults in the United States (Cohen et al., 2011; Machado and Diehl, 2016; Rinella and Sanyal, 2016; Wree et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The expansion of adipose tissue in obese individuals is strongly associated with the development of NAFLD.
source: The expansion of adipose tissue in obese individuals is strongly associated with the development of NAFLD, yet mechanisms linking obesity to NAFLD and more advanced forms of liver disease such as NASH and cirrhosis are not well understood (Cohen et al., 2011; Machado and Diehl, 2016; Rinella and Sanyal, 2016; Wree et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Mechanisms linking obesity to NAFLD and more advanced forms of liver disease such as NASH and cirrhosis are not well understood.
source: The expansion of adipose tissue in obese individuals is strongly associated with the development of NAFLD, yet mechanisms linking obesity to NAFLD and more advanced forms of liver disease such as NASH and cirrhosis are not well understood (Cohen et al., 2011; Machado and Diehl, 2016; Rinella and Sanyal, 2016; Wree et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies and represents a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) provide a powerful unbiased tool to identify new genes and pathways that are involved in human disease.
source: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) provide a powerful unbiased tool to identify new genes and pathways that are involved in human disease, allowing for pinpoint accuracy in identification of new drug targets.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about GWAS methodology.

claim: Human genetic studies led to rapid development of monoclonal antibodies targeting PCSK9 for hyperlipidemia and cardiovascular disease.
source: This is exemplified by the recent success story of human genetic studies leading to rapid development of monoclonal antibodies targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) for hyperlipidemia and cardiovascular disease (Hess et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: The rs641738 variant is a C > T missense single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) within the first exon of the TMC4 gene.
source: The rs641738 variant is associated with a C > T missense single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) within the first exon the TMC4 gene, yet available data suggest that TMC4 is not abundantly expressed in human liver (Mancina et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: TMC4 is not abundantly expressed in human liver.
source: The rs641738 variant is associated with a C > T missense single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) within the first exon the TMC4 gene, yet available data suggest that TMC4 is not abundantly expressed in human liver (Mancina et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: Reduced expression and activity of MBOAT7 may be mechanistically linked to liver disease progression.
source: Based on eQTL studies in the liver it has been suggested that instead reduced expression and activity of MBOAT7 may be mechanistically linked to liver disease progression (Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; International Liver Disease Genetics Consortium et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies and eQTL analysis.

claim: MBOAT7 encodes an acyltransferase enzyme that specifically esterifies arachidonyl-CoA to lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) to generate the predominant molecular species of phosphatidylinositol (PI) in cell membranes (38:4).
source: The MBOAT7 gene encodes an acyltransferase enzyme that specifically esterifies arachidonyl-CoA to lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) to generate the predominant molecular species of phosphatidylinositol (PI) in cell membranes (38:4) (Gijón et al., 2008; Zarini et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2012; Anderson et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies describing MBOAT7 biochemical activity.

claim: MBOAT7 is a unique contributor to the Lands' cycle.
source: Given this biochemical activity, MBOAT7 is a unique contributor to the Lands' cycle, which is a series of phospholipase-driven deacylation and lysophospholipid acyltransferase-driven reacylation reactions that synergize to alter phospholipid fatty acid composition, creating membrane asymmetry and diversity (Shindou and Shimizu, 2009; Shindou et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies and knowledge about the Lands' cycle.

claim: MBOAT7, unlike other lysophospholipid acyltransferases, only diversifies the fatty acid composition of membrane PI species and not phospholipids with other head groups.
source: It is important to note that MBOAT7, unlike other lysophospholipid acyltransferases, only diversifies the fatty acid composition of membrane PI species and not phospholipids with other head groups (Gijón et al., 2008; Zarini et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2012; Anderson et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies describing MBOAT7 substrate specificity.

claim: There is no information regarding how MBOAT7 activity or its substrate (LPI) or product (PI) lipids impact liver disease progression.
source: Despite recent progress in characterizing the selective biochemistry of MBOAT7 (Gijón et al., 2008), and the clear genetic links to liver disease (Buch et al., 2015; Mancina et al., 2016; Luukkonen et al., 2016; International Liver Disease Genetics Consortium et al., 2016; Viitasalo et al., 2016; Krawczyk et al., 2017; Thabet et al., 2017), there is no information regarding how MBOAT7 activity or its substrate (LPI) or product (PI) lipids impact liver disease progression.
evidence: The claim represents a knowledge gap in the field at the time of the study.

claim: MBOAT7 expression is suppressed in obese humans and rodents.
source: Here, we demonstrate that MBOAT7 expression is suppressed in obese humans and rodents.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing reduced MBOAT7 expression in obese subjects and animal models.

claim: Mboat7 substrate lipids (LPIs) may be critical mediators of obesity-linked liver disease progression.
source: Here, we demonstrate that MBOAT7 expression is suppressed in obese humans and rodents. Furthermore, we show that Mboat7, but not Tmc4, loss of function in mice is sufficient to drive NAFLD progression, and show that Mboat7 substrate lipids (LPIs) may be critical mediators of obesity-linked liver disease progression.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that LPI administration promotes inflammatory and fibrotic gene expression in Mboat7 knockdown mice.

claim: NAFLD progression is commonly associated with obesity.
source: NAFLD progression is commonly associated with obesity, and it has even been suggested that obesity is a causative factor in the pathogenesis of NAFLD (Younossi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: Obesity is a causative factor in the pathogenesis of NAFLD.
source: NAFLD progression is commonly associated with obesity, and it has even been suggested that obesity is a causative factor in the pathogenesis of NAFLD (Younossi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: The common MBOAT7 SNP (rs641738) is associated with NAFLD.
source: Although, there is now strong support that the common MBOAT7 SNP (rs641738) is associated with NAFLD, it is not known whether MBOAT7 expression is significantly altered in obese people.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies mentioned earlier in the manuscript.

claim: It is not known whether MBOAT7 expression is significantly altered in obese people.
source: Although, there is now strong support that the common MBOAT7 SNP (rs641738) is associated with NAFLD, it is not known whether MBOAT7 expression is significantly altered in obese people.
evidence: The claim represents a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Hepatic MBOAT7 expression was dramatically reduced in obese people, when compared to normal weight controls.
source: We found that hepatic MBOAT7 expression was dramatically reduced in obese people, when compared to normal weight controls (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The striking reduction in MBOAT7 expression in obese subjects was not due to presence of the rs641738 MBOAT7 SNP.
source: It is important to note that this striking reduction in MBOAT7 expression was not due to presence of the rs641738 MBOAT7 SNP, as we found the minor allele frequency was quite similar in lean, obese, and severely obese subjects (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing similar minor allele frequencies across BMI groups in Figure 1A.

claim: The minor allele frequency of rs641738 was quite similar in lean, obese, and severely obese subjects.
source: It is important to note that this striking reduction in MBOAT7 expression was not due to presence of the rs641738 MBOAT7 SNP, as we found the minor allele frequency was quite similar in lean, obese, and severely obese subjects (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Mboat7 expression was reduced in ob/ob mice compared to lean WT controls.
source: Mboat7 expression was reduced in ob/ob mice compared to lean WT controls (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: High fat diet-induced obesity in Sprague-Dawley rats was associated with significant reductions in hepatic Mboat7 expression.
source: In agreement, we found that high fat diet-induced obesity in Sprague-Dawley rats was also associated with significant reductions in hepatic Mboat7 expression (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Hepatic expression of MBOAT7 is suppressed in obese humans and rodents.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that hepatic expression of MBOAT7 is suppressed in obese humans and rodents.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from human, mouse, and rat studies.

claim: Mboat7 expression in the liver was only modestly correlated (r = −0.244, p=0.01) with adiposity across strains in the HMDP.
source: Across the different strains in the HMDP, we found that Mboat7 expression in the liver was only modestly correlated (r = −0.244, p=0.01) with adiposity (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the HMDP shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mboat7 expression in white adipose tissue was strongly negatively correlated (r = −0.68, p=2.3e-15) with both fat pad weight and % body fat in male and female mice in the HMDP.
source: However, Mboat7 expression in white adipose tissue (WAT) was strongly negatively correlated (r = −0.68, p=2.3e-15) with both fat pad weight and % body fat in male and female mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the HMDP shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Expression of Mboat7 in adipose tissue was negatively (r = −0.38, p=0.0002) associated with indices of insulin sensitivity in the HMDP.
source: We found that expression of Mboat7 in adipose tissue was negatively (r = −0.38, p=0.0002) associated with indices of insulin sensitivity (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the HMDP shown in Figure 1F.

claim: MBOAT7 may be mechanistically linked to the well-known association between obesity, insulin resistance, and NAFLD progression.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that MBOAT7 may be mechanistically linked to the well-known association between obesity, insulin resistance, and NAFLD progression.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the correlation data presented.

claim: Global Mboat7-/- mice are only viable for several weeks after birth due to the critical role Mboat7 plays in cortical lamination and neuronal migration in the brain.
source: Metabolic phenotyping of global Mboat7-/- mice has been limited due to the fact that these mice are only viable for several weeks after birth due to the critical role Mboat7 plays in cortical lamination and neuronal migration in the brain (Lee et al., 2012; Anderson et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Second-generation antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) predominately target liver, adipose tissue, and cells within the reticuloendothelial system.
source: To overcome this barrier, we have generated second-generation antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), which predominately target liver, adipose tissue, and cells within the reticuloendothelial system to selectively knock down Mboat7 expression in adult mice using methods we have previously described (Schugar et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study and knowledge about ASO technology.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment resulted in significant reductions of Mboat7 mRNA and protein in the liver.
source: Mboat7 ASO treatment resulted in significant reductions of Mboat7 mRNA and protein in the liver (Figure 2A), and white adipose tissue (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), without altering Mboat7 expression in the brain, spleen, heart, or skeletal muscle (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment significantly reduced Mboat7 expression in white adipose tissue.
source: Mboat7 ASO treatment resulted in significant reductions of Mboat7 mRNA and protein in the liver (Figure 2A), and white adipose tissue (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), without altering Mboat7 expression in the brain, spleen, heart, or skeletal muscle (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not alter Mboat7 expression in the brain, spleen, heart, or skeletal muscle.
source: Mboat7 ASO treatment resulted in significant reductions of Mboat7 mRNA and protein in the liver (Figure 2A), and white adipose tissue (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), without altering Mboat7 expression in the brain, spleen, heart, or skeletal muscle (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not alter body weight.
source: Although Mboat7 ASO treatment significantly reduced adipose Mboat7 expression (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this was not associated with alterations in body weight (Figure 2B), fat mass (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L), adipose gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K), food intake (Figure 2C), energy expenditure (Figure 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3), or physical activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not alter fat mass.
source: Although Mboat7 ASO treatment significantly reduced adipose Mboat7 expression (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this was not associated with alterations in body weight (Figure 2B), fat mass (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L), adipose gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K), food intake (Figure 2C), energy expenditure (Figure 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3), or physical activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1L.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not alter adipose gene expression.
source: Although Mboat7 ASO treatment significantly reduced adipose Mboat7 expression (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this was not associated with alterations in body weight (Figure 2B), fat mass (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L), adipose gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K), food intake (Figure 2C), energy expenditure (Figure 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3), or physical activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not alter food intake.
source: Although Mboat7 ASO treatment significantly reduced adipose Mboat7 expression (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this was not associated with alterations in body weight (Figure 2B), fat mass (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L), adipose gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K), food intake (Figure 2C), energy expenditure (Figure 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3), or physical activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not alter energy expenditure.
source: Although Mboat7 ASO treatment significantly reduced adipose Mboat7 expression (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this was not associated with alterations in body weight (Figure 2B), fat mass (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L), adipose gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K), food intake (Figure 2C), energy expenditure (Figure 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3), or physical activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not alter physical activity.
source: Although Mboat7 ASO treatment significantly reduced adipose Mboat7 expression (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), this was not associated with alterations in body weight (Figure 2B), fat mass (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L), adipose gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–K), food intake (Figure 2C), energy expenditure (Figure 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3), or physical activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown resulted in an increase in liver weight.
source: Despite this lack of phenotypic differences in adipose tissue, Mboat7 knockdown resulted in large alterations in the liver lipid storage. Mboat7 ASO treatment promoted an increase in liver weight (Figure 2F) and striking hepatic steatosis in HFD-fed, but not chow-fed mice (Figure 2E,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment promoted striking hepatic steatosis in HFD-fed, but not chow-fed mice.
source: Despite this lack of phenotypic differences in adipose tissue, Mboat7 knockdown resulted in large alterations in the liver lipid storage. Mboat7 ASO treatment promoted an increase in liver weight (Figure 2F) and striking hepatic steatosis in HFD-fed, but not chow-fed mice (Figure 2E,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and 2I.

claim: Mboat7 ASO-driven hepatic steatosis was consistently seen with two distinct ASOs targeting different regions of the Mboat7 messenger RNA.
source: Importantly, Mboat7 ASO-driven hepatic steatosis was consistently seen with two distinct ASOs targeting different regions of the Mboat7 messenger RNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Mboat7 ASO-driven hepatic steatosis was characterized by accumulation of triglycerides, free cholesterol, and cholesterol esters only in high fat fed cohorts.
source: Mboat7 ASO-driven hepatic steatosis was characterized by accumulation of triglycerides, free cholesterol, and cholesterol esters only in high fat fed cohorts (Figure 2J–M).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J–M.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown did not dramatically alter the levels of triglycerides or cholesterol in circulating lipoproteins.
source: Despite these significant alterations in hepatic lipids, Mboat7 knockdown did not dramatically alter the levels of triglycerides or cholesterol in circulating lipoproteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown was associated with hepatocyte injury as indicated by elevated liver enzyme levels (AST and ALT), but this only occurred in high fat-fed mice.
source: Mboat7 knockdown was also associated with hepatocyte injury as indicated by elevated liver enzyme levels (AST and ALT), but this only occurred in high fat-fed mice (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and 2H.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown resulted in 124 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) being suppressed and 887 DEGs being upregulated.
source: Mboat7 knockdown resulted in a number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with 124 DEGs being suppressed and 887 DEGs being upregulated by Mboat7 ASO treatment (top 50 DEGs shown in Figure 3B and overall changes in Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: Many of the pathways that were significantly enriched by Mboat7 knockdown are mechanistically linked to liver injury such as leukocyte extravasation, monocyte/macrophage activation, and fibrosis/hepatic stellate cell activation.
source: To understand the major pathways affected by Mboat7 knockdown, we performed Gene Ontology Molecular Function enrichment analysis, and found that many of the pathways that were significantly enriched are mechanistically linked to liver injury such as leukocyte extravasation, monocyte/macrophage activation, and fibrosis/hepatic stellate cell activation (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Mboat7 mRNA levels were dramatically suppressed by Mboat7 ASO treatment.
source: As predicted Mboat7 mRNA levels were dramatically suppressed by Mboat7 ASO treatment, but quite unexpectedly we also saw that the expression of Tmc4 was reduced in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice (Figure 3B,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing and qPCR data shown in Figure 3B and 3E.

claim: The expression of Tmc4 was reduced in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice.
source: As predicted Mboat7 mRNA levels were dramatically suppressed by Mboat7 ASO treatment, but quite unexpectedly we also saw that the expression of Tmc4 was reduced in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice (Figure 3B,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing and qPCR data shown in Figure 3B and 3E.

claim: ASO-mediated knockdown of Mboat7 results in coordinated suppression of its neighboring gene Tmc4.
source: These data shown for the first time that ASO-mediated knockdown of Mboat7 results in coordinated suppression of its neighboring gene Tmc4 (the rs641738 polymorphism is located in exon 1 of the TMC4 gene), indicating some potential cross talk that deserves further exploration (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown resulted in elevated expression of genes associated with inflammation (Tnfa and Il1b) and early fibrosis (Col1a2 and Acta2) in high fat fed mice.
source: Quantitative real time PCR (qPCR) analysis also confirmed the RNA sequencing results showing that Mboat7 knockdown resulted in elevated expression of gene associated with inflammation (Tnfa and Il1b) and early fibrosis (Col1a2 and Acta2) in high fat fed mice (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown increased Cd8+ T lymphocytes in the liver.
source: In addition, Mboat7 knockdown was associated with altered immune cell populations in the liver. Mboat7 knockdown increased Cd8+ T lymphocytes, while decreasing the total number of Cd11b+ macrophages in the liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown decreased the total number of Cd11b+ macrophages in the liver.
source: In addition, Mboat7 knockdown was associated with altered immune cell populations in the liver. Mboat7 knockdown increased Cd8+ T lymphocytes, while decreasing the total number of Cd11b+ macrophages in the liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Of the hepatic macrophages that were present in Mboat7 knockdown mice, more were skewed towards the proinflammatory M1 (Cd11c+) state, and less were skewed towards the alternative M2 (Cd206+) phenotype.
source: Of the hepatic macrophages that were present, more were skewed towards the proinflammatory M1 (Cd11c+) state, and less were skewed towards the alternative M2 (Cd206+) phenotype (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Under high fat feeding conditions, Mboat7 loss of function is associated with dysregulated immune cell homeostasis, inflammation, and gene expression signatures that are consistent with early activation of pro-fibrotic programs in the liver.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that specifically under high fat feeding conditions, Mboat7 loss of function is associated with dysregulated immune cell homeostasis, inflammation, and gene expression signatures that are consistent with early activation of pro-fibrotic programs in the liver (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in Figure 3 and related supplements.

claim: Global Tmc4 knockout mice have marked reductions in hepatic Tmc4 mRNA.
source: Global Tmc4 knockout mice have marked reductions in hepatic Tmc4 mRNA (Figure 4A) and protein (Figure 4B), yet importantly Mboat7 expression is unaltered (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Global Tmc4 knockout mice have marked reductions in hepatic Tmc4 protein.
source: Global Tmc4 knockout mice have marked reductions in hepatic Tmc4 mRNA (Figure 4A) and protein (Figure 4B), yet importantly Mboat7 expression is unaltered (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Mboat7 expression is unaltered in global Tmc4 knockout mice.
source: Global Tmc4 knockout mice have marked reductions in hepatic Tmc4 mRNA (Figure 4A) and protein (Figure 4B), yet importantly Mboat7 expression is unaltered (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Tmc4 null mice show similar levels of hepatic lipids when fed a high fat diet compared to wild type mice.
source: In contrast to the striking hepatic steatosis seen with Mboat7 loss of function (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 4), Tmc4 null mice show similar levels of hepatic lipids when fed a high fat diet (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mboat7, but not Tmc4, is the primary mediator of hepatic steatosis seen with the rs641738 variant or in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice.
source: These data strongly implicate Mboat7, but not Tmc4, as the primary mediator of hepatic steatosis seen with the rs641738 variant or in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data comparing Mboat7 and Tmc4 loss of function.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown was associated with significantly impaired systemic glucose tolerance.
source: Mboat7 knockdown was associated with significantly impaired systemic glucose tolerance (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Mboat7 ASO-treated mice exhibited profound hyperinsulinemia in the fasted state and throughout an intraperitoneal glucose tolerance test.
source: Mboat7 ASO-treated mice also exhibited profound hyperinsulinemia in the fasted state and throughout an intraperitoneal glucose tolerance test (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Glucose-stimulated C-peptide release was elevated in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, potentially indicating overproduction of insulin in the pancreatic β-cell.
source: In parallel, glucose-stimulated C-peptide release was elevated in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, potentially indicating overproduction of insulin in the pancreatic β-cell (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and inference about β-cell function.

claim: During an intraperitoneal insulin tolerance test, Mboat7 ASO-treated mice showed blunted plasma glucose lowering.
source: During an intraperitoneal insulin tolerance test, Mboat7 ASO-treated mice showed blunted plasma glucose lowering (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Mboat7 ASO-treated mice had reduced insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of IR and downstream Akt in the liver.
source: Mboat7 ASO-treated mice had reduced insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of IR and downstream Akt in the liver (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter insulin signal transduction in either skeletal muscle or white adipose tissue.
source: However, Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter insulin signal transduction in either skeletal muscle or white adipose tissue (Figure 5F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and 5G.

claim: ASO-mediated knockdown of Mboat7 promotes hyperinsulinemia, yet impairs insulin action specifically in the liver.
source: These data suggest that ASO-mediated knockdown of Mboat7 promotes hyperinsulinemia, yet impairs insulin action specifically in the liver.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data on glucose homeostasis and insulin signaling.

claim: In chow fed mice Mboat7 knockdown only modestly decreased hepatic LPIAT activity toward 18:1 LPI.
source: In chow fed mice Mboat7 knockdown only modestly decreased hepatic LPIAT activity toward 18:1 LPI (Figure 6A), yet in high fat diet-challenged mice Mboat7 knockdown resulted in a highly significant ~50% reduction in LPIAT activity using either 16:0, 18:0, or 18:1 LPI substrates (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In high fat diet-challenged mice Mboat7 knockdown resulted in a highly significant ~50% reduction in LPIAT activity using either 16:0, 18:0, or 18:1 LPI substrates.
source: In chow fed mice Mboat7 knockdown only modestly decreased hepatic LPIAT activity toward 18:1 LPI (Figure 6A), yet in high fat diet-challenged mice Mboat7 knockdown resulted in a highly significant ~50% reduction in LPIAT activity using either 16:0, 18:0, or 18:1 LPI substrates (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Mboat7 is a significant contributor to total hepatic LPIAT activity, especially under high fat feeding conditions.
source: These data suggest that Mboat7 is a significant contributor to total hepatic LPIAT activity, especially under high fat feeding conditions.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the LPIAT activity data.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter LPI levels in the circulation.
source: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter LPI levels in the circulation, but was associated with selective reduction in the 38:3 and 38:4 species of circulating PI lipids (Figure 6B, Figure 6C, and Figure 6—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment was associated with selective reduction in the 38:3 and 38:4 species of circulating PI lipids.
source: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter LPI levels in the circulation, but was associated with selective reduction in the 38:3 and 38:4 species of circulating PI lipids (Figure 6B, Figure 6C, and Figure 6—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown was associated with significant accumulation of 16:0 and 18:1 LPI species in the liver.
source: In contrast to effects in the circulation, Mboat7 knockdown was associated with significant accumulation of 16:0 and 18:1 LPI species in the liver (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mboat7 ASO-treatment resulted in reduced 38:3 and 38:4 PI levels, while increasing more saturated (34:1, 34:2, 36:1, and 36:2) PI species in the liver.
source: Furthermore, Mboat7 ASO-treatment resulted in reduced 38:3 and 38:4 PI levels, while increasing more saturated (34:1, 34:2, 36:1, and 36:2) PI species in the liver (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In white adipose tissue, Mboat7 knockdown did not significantly alter LPI levels.
source: In white adipose tissue, Mboat7 knockdown did not significantly alter LPI levels (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), but promoted marked accumulation of more saturated PI species both in chow and high fat fed mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown promoted marked accumulation of more saturated PI species in white adipose tissue both in chow and high fat fed mice.
source: In white adipose tissue, Mboat7 knockdown did not significantly alter LPI levels (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), but promoted marked accumulation of more saturated PI species both in chow and high fat fed mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment resulted in significant reductions in several PUFA-enriched PI species (38:3, 38:4, 38:5, and 38:6) in adipose tissue.
source: Also, Mboat7 ASO treatment resulted in significant reductions in several PUFA-enriched PI species (38:3, 38:4, 38:5, and 38:6) in adipose tissue (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter LPI or PI levels in the brain.
source: In contrast to alterations in LPI and PI levels in liver and adipose tissue (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplements 1–2), Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter LPI or PI levels in the brain (Figure 6—figure supplement 3) or pancreas (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter LPI or PI levels in the pancreas.
source: In contrast to alterations in LPI and PI levels in liver and adipose tissue (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplements 1–2), Mboat7 ASO treatment did not significantly alter LPI or PI levels in the brain (Figure 6—figure supplement 3) or pancreas (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown did not significantly alter the hepatic levels of other major phospholipids including phosphatidylcholines, lysophosphatidylcholines, phosphatidylethanolamines, lysophosphatidylethanolamines, phosphatidylserines, phosphatidylglycerols, or phosphatidic acids.
source: In contrast to marked changes in inositol-containing phospholipids, it is also important to note that Mboat7 knockdown did not significantly alter the hepatic levels of other major phospholipids including phosphatidylcholines, lysophosphatidylcholines, phosphatidylethanolamines, lysophosphatidylethanolamines, phosphatidylserines, phosphatidylglycerols, or phosphatidic acids (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5.

claim: ASO-mediated knockdown of Mboat7 primarily alters LPI and PI levels in the liver and white adipose tissue.
source: Collectively, these data show that ASO-mediated knockdown of Mboat7 primarily alters LPI and PI levels in the liver and white adipose tissue, which creates the potential to induce an imbalance of local lipid mediators that originate from PI metabolism.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the lipidomics data across multiple tissues.

claim: When arachidonic acid-derived pro-inflammatory (LTB4, PGE2, PGD2, PGF2α, and TXB2) and pro-resolving (15R-LXA4) lipid mediators were examined there was no apparent alteration in the liver of Mboat7 ASO-treated mice.
source: However, when we examined arachidonic acid-derived pro-inflammatory (LTB4, PGE2, PGD2, PGF2α, and TXB2) and pro-resolving (15R-LXA4) lipid mediators there was no apparent alteration in the liver of Mboat7 ASO-treated mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 6.

claim: The data do not support a rate-limiting role for MBOAT7 in arachidonic acid-derived lipid mediator production in mice.
source: Collectively, these data do not support a rate-limiting role for MBOAT7 in arachidonic acid-derived lipid mediator production in mice.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the lipid mediator data.

claim: Saturated LPI lipids are significantly elevated in the circulation of humans with advanced fibrosis compared to healthy controls.
source: In further support of this concept, we found that saturated LPI lipids are significantly elevated in the circulation of humans with advanced fibrosis compared to healthy controls (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Injection of 16:0, 18:0, or 18:1 LPI into control ASO-treated mice did not alter hepatic inflammatory or fibrotic gene expression.
source: Injection of 16:0, 18:0, or 18:1 LPI into control ASO-treated mice did not alter hepatic inflammatory or fibrotic gene expression (Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Exogenously provided LPI is rapidly esterified into membrane PI pools.
source: This is not surprising, given that it was previously reported that exogenously provided LPI is rapidly esterified into membrane PI pools (Darnell and Saltiel, 1991; Darnell et al., 1991; Jackson and Parton, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Under normal conditions MBOAT7 activity rapidly acylates LPI to divert this signaling lipid into a membrane PI storage pool.
source: In other words, under normal conditions MBOAT7 activity rapidly acylates LPI to divert this signaling lipid into a membrane PI storage pool.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the known biochemical activity of MBOAT7 and cited studies.

claim: Under conditions such as obesity where Mboat7 activity is diminished, LPI-driven signaling can be sustained and promote liver injury.
source: We next postulated that under conditions such as obesity where Mboat7 activity is diminished, LPI-driven signaling can be sustained and promote liver injury.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Direct injection of exogenous 18 carbon LPIs can rapidly (24 hr) increase the expression of genes characteristic of hepatic inflammation (Cd11c, Tnfa, IL1b) and early fibrosis (Desmin, Col1A1, Col1A2, and Acta2) in mice with Mboat7 knockdown.
source: In support of this concept, direct injection of exogenous 18 carbon LPIs can rapidly (24 hr) increase the expression of genes characteristic of hepatic inflammation (Cd11c, Tnfa, IL1b) and early fibrosis (Desmin, Col1A1, Col1A2, and Acta2) in mice with Mboat7 knockdown (Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: 18 carbon LPI lipids can acutely induce hepatic inflammatory and fibrotic gene expression programs, but only when MBOAT7 function is compromised, as is seen in obesity or with loss of function variants like rs641738.
source: These data suggest that 18 carbon LPI lipids can acutely induce hepatic inflammatory and fibrotic gene expression programs, but only when MBOAT7 function is compromised, as is seen in obesity or with loss of function variants like rs641738.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: 18 carbon LPI lipids can only significantly elicit pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic effects in high fat fed mice.
source: It is important to note that 18 carbon LPI lipids can only significantly elicit such pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic effects in high fat fed mice (Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2), as we did not see this same effect in chow fed cohorts (not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: A small subset of acute phase response genes (serum amyloid A genes, Saa1 and Saa2) and other immunomodulatory genes (Gdf15, Ly6d, Lcn2, Socs2, etc.) were altered by 18:0 LPI treatment in a Mboat7-dependent manner.
source: Although direct administration of 18 carbon LPI lipids in chow fed mice did not significantly alter the same pro-inflammatory or pro-fibrotic genes as we found with Mboat7 knockdown (Figure 3), we did find that a small subset of acute phase response genes (serum amyloid A genes, Saa1 and Saa2) and other immunomodulatory genes (Gdf15, Ly6d, Lcn2, Socs2, etc.) were altered by 18:0 LPI treatment in a Mboat7-dependent manner (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: When liver triacylglycerol levels were examined in the LPI injection experiment, significantly elevation was found in the saline and 18:1 LPI injection groups, but not in the 16:0 LPI injection group.
source: Interestingly, when liver triacylglycerol levels were examined in this LPI injection experiment, we only found significantly elevation in the saline and 18:1 LPI injection groups, but not in the 16:0 LPI injection group (Figure 8I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: 18 carbon LPI lipids can alter hepatic inflammatory transcriptional programs, but this is highly reliant on both diminished Mboat7 expression/activity and high fat diet feeding.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that 18 carbon LPI lipids can alter hepatic inflammatory transcriptional programs, but this is highly reliant on both diminished Mboat7 expression/activity and high fat diet feeding.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown did not alter lipogenic gene expression either in the fed or fasted state.
source: Unlike many other models of hepatic steatosis, there were no significant alterations in lipogenic gene expression either in the fed or fasted state with Mboat7 knockdown (Figure 9A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The expression of carnitine palmitoyl transferase 1 (Cpt1) was significantly elevated with Mboat7 knockdown.
source: Unexpectedly, the expression of carnitine palmitoyl transferase 1 (Cpt1) was significantly elevated with Mboat7 knockdown (Figure 9A), but this would not be expected to promote the accumulation of neutral lipids.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The expression of enzymes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (Hmgcr and Hmcgs1) were modestly reduced in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, but only in the fasted state.
source: The expression of enzymes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (Hmgcr and Hmcgs1) were modestly reduced in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, but only in the fasted state (Figure 9A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Expression of the cholesterol efflux regulator Abca1 was elevated in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, but only in the fasted state.
source: In addition, expression of the cholesterol efflux regulator Abca1 was elevated in Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, but only in the fasted state.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data mentioned in the text.

claim: Mboat7 ASO-treated mice did not have significant differences in VLDL-TG secretion during a detergent block.
source: Next, we evaluated whether Mboat7 may influence the export of neutral lipids via packaging on nascent very low density lipoproteins (VLDL). However, Mboat7 ASO-treated mice did not have significant differences in VLDL-TG secretion during a detergent block (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown did not alter basal or catecholamine-stimulated adipocyte lipolysis in vivo.
source: However, Mboat7 knockdown did not alter basal or catecholamine-stimulated adipocyte lipolysis in vivo (Figure 9C), ruling out a role for altered adipose lipolysis as a contributing factor.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: MBOAT7 can localize to cytosolic lipid droplets.
source: Finally, we examined the possibility that MBOAT7 may be a determinate of metabolism locally at the surface of cytosolic lipid droplets to regulate hepatic steatosis, given that one recent study reported that MBOAT7 can localize to cytosolic lipid droplets (Mancina et al., 2016). We confirmed that MBOAT7 can indeed be found in lipid droplets isolated by sucrose gradient fractionation (Figure 9F), and plays a regulatory role in both the lipidome and proteome of cytosolic lipid droplets.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study and experimental data shown in Figure 9F.

claim: Cytosolic lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice showed marked accumulation of 18:0 LPI and 20:4 LPI, but not 16:0 LPI or 18:1 LPI.
source: Cytosolic lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice showed marked accumulation of 18:0 LPI and 20:4 LPI, but not 16:0 LPI or 18:1 LPI (Figure 9D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: Lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice have a reduced level of 38:4 PI but a reciprocal increase in 36:3 and 38:3 PI.
source: Also, lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice have a reduced level of 38:4 PI but a reciprocal increase in 36:3 and 38:3 PI (Figure 9E), which is quite different when to compared to effects in whole liver (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: Mboat7 knockdown is associated with accumulation of several proteins involved in lipid synthesis and storage on isolated lipid droplets.
source: In addition to alterations in the lipid droplet lipidome, Mboat7 knockdown is associated with accumulation of several proteins involved in lipid synthesis and storage on isolated lipid droplets (Figure 9F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9F.

claim: Both perilipin 2 and 3 (PLIN2 and PLIN3) were much more abundant on lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice.
source: Both perilipin 2 and 3 (PLIN2 and PLIN3) were much more abundant on lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, as were the critical lipid synthetic enzymes CTP:phosphocholine cytidylyltransferase α (CCTα) and glycerol-3-phosphate 4 (GPAT4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data mentioned in the text.

claim: The critical lipid synthetic enzymes CTP:phosphocholine cytidylyltransferase α (CCTα) and glycerol-3-phosphate 4 (GPAT4) were much more abundant on lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice.
source: Both perilipin 2 and 3 (PLIN2 and PLIN3) were much more abundant on lipid droplets isolated from Mboat7 ASO-treated mice, as were the critical lipid synthetic enzymes CTP:phosphocholine cytidylyltransferase α (CCTα) and glycerol-3-phosphate 4 (GPAT4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data mentioned in the text.

claim: Lipid droplet targeting of CCTα and GPAT4 are critical regulators of the overall size and triglyceride storage capacity of lipid droplets.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Huh7 cells lacking MBOAT7 have increased lipid droplets upon fatty acid loading.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10A and 10B.

claim: Lipid accumulation in MBOAT7-deficient Huh7 cells was due in part to increases in de novo lipogenesis rates.
source: This lipid accumulation was due in part to increases in de novo lipogenesis rates (Figure 10C), and reciprocal decreases in fatty acid oxidation rates (Figure 10D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Lipid accumulation in MBOAT7-deficient Huh7 cells was due in part to reciprocal decreases in fatty acid oxidation rates.
source: This lipid accumulation was due in part to increases in de novo lipogenesis rates (Figure 10C), and reciprocal decreases in fatty acid oxidation rates (Figure 10D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: MBOAT7-deficient Huh7 cells did not have altered turnover of stored triacylglycerol.
source: However, MBOAT-deficient Huh7 cells did not have altered turnover of stored triacylglycerol (Figure 10E) or cholesterol ester (Figure 10F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10E.

claim: MBOAT7-deficient Huh7 cells did not have altered turnover of stored cholesterol ester.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10F.

claim: Genetic deletion of Tmc4 does not alter hepatic lipid storage.
source: The major findings of the current study include the following: (1) Genetic deletion of Tmc4 does not alter hepatic lipid storage, (2) Hepatic expression of MBOAT7 is reduced in obese humans and rodents, independent of rs641738 status, (3) Mboat7 expression in mouse liver and adipose tissue is negatively correlated with obesity and insulin sensitivity across the strains represented in the Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel, (4) Mboat7 knockdown promotes hepatic steatosis, hepatocyte death, inflammation, and early gene expression profiles consistent with fibrosis, but this only happens when mice are challenged with a high fat diet, (5) Mboat7 loss of function promotes striking hyperinsulinemia and hepatic insulin resistance, (6) Mboat7 knockdown results in tissue-specific reorganization of its substrates (LPI) and product (PI) lipids, (7) LPI lipids can rapidly induce hepatic inflammatory and fibrotic gene expression programs in an Mboat7-dependent manner in mice, and (8) the hepatic steatosis seen with Mboat7 knockdown is not related to differences in lipogenic gene expression, VLDL secretion, or tissue lipolysis, but instead may be related to alterations in hepatic lipid droplet accumulation of lipogenic enzymes (CCTα and GPAT4) that allow for expansion of large lipid droplets (Guo et al., 2008; Krahmer et al., 2011; Wilfling et al., 2013), and increased rates of de novo lipogenesis and reduced fatty acid oxidation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The hepatic steatosis seen with Mboat7 knockdown may be related to alterations in hepatic lipid droplet accumulation of lipogenic enzymes (CCTα and GPAT4) that allow for expansion of large lipid droplets, and increased rates of de novo lipogenesis and reduced fatty acid oxidation.
source: The major findings of the current study include the following: (1) Genetic deletion of Tmc4 does not alter hepatic lipid storage, (2) Hepatic expression of MBOAT7 is reduced in obese humans and rodents, independent of rs641738 status, (3) Mboat7 expression in mouse liver and adipose tissue is negatively correlated with obesity and insulin sensitivity across the strains represented in the Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel, (4) Mboat7 knockdown promotes hepatic steatosis, hepatocyte death, inflammation, and early gene expression profiles consistent with fibrosis, but this only happens when mice are challenged with a high fat diet, (5) Mboat7 loss of function promotes striking hyperinsulinemia and hepatic insulin resistance, (6) Mboat7 knockdown results in tissue-specific reorganization of its substrates (LPI) and product (PI) lipids, (7) LPI lipids can rapidly induce hepatic inflammatory and fibrotic gene expression programs in an Mboat7-dependent manner in mice, and (8) the hepatic steatosis seen with Mboat7 knockdown is not related to differences in lipogenic gene expression, VLDL secretion, or tissue lipolysis, but instead may be related to alterations in hepatic lipid droplet accumulation of lipogenic enzymes (CCTα and GPAT4) that allow for expansion of large lipid droplets (Guo et al., 2008; Krahmer et al., 2011; Wilfling et al., 2013), and increased rates of de novo lipogenesis and reduced fatty acid oxidation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript and citations to published studies.

claim: Mboat7-driven acylation of LPI lipids is an important modulator of both liver disease progression and associated type 2 diabetes.
source: Collectively, these studies identify MBOAT7-driven acylation of LPI lipids as an important modulator of both liver disease progression and associated type 2 diabetes.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the overall experimental findings.
